title: Message-passing graph persistence
abstract: arXiv:2611.06801v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Message-passing graph neural networks (GNNs) are limited in expressive power by the one-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman test. Persistent homology (PH) provides topological descriptors that can complement GNN representations, but existing approaches typically compute persistence separately from the representation learning process. In this paper, we introduce Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), a family of topological descriptors that incorporates message passing into graph filtrations. At each filtration step, node embeddings are updated using the current subgraph and associated with persistence events. These embeddings also determine the representatives of connected components during persistence computation. We prove that MGP is invariant under graph isomorphism and that it is strictly more expressive than the PH-based descriptors it extends. We evaluate MGP on an expressivity benchmark and on several graph classification and regress

translated_abstract: 消息传递图神经网络的表达能力受限于其一维Weisfeiler-Leman测试。持久同调提供了可以补充GNN表示的拓扑描述子，但现有方法通常将持久性的计算与表示学习过程分开进行。在本文中，我们提出了消息传递图持久性，这是一类将消息传递机制融入图过滤过程的拓扑描述子。在每个过滤步骤中，节点嵌入利用当前子图进行更新，并与持久性事件相关联。这些嵌入还在持久性计算过程中决定连通分量的代表元。我们证明了MGP在图同构下保持不变，并且其表达能力严格强于其所扩展的基于持久同调的描述子。我们在表达能力基准测试以及多个图分类和回归任务上对MGP进行了评估。
tldr: 本文提出消息传递图持久性（MGP），将消息传递机制融入图过滤过程构建拓扑描述子，并证明了其图同构不变性以及严格强于现有基于持久同调描述子的表达能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Message-Passing Graph Persistence (MGP), a family of topological descriptors that integrates message passing into graph filtrations, proving it is isomorphism-invariant and strictly more expressive than existing PH-based descriptors.
